meta.title: ON NON-FIRM RISK
meta.subtitle: A transformation thesis on interruptible power and the insurance gap

III · Can the form carry it
XII · The wedge, not the product

blocks.text: London underwrites interruption as if it required damage. Curtailment is contractual and register-native — hourly economics on one ledger, multi-year damage-BI on the other — yet renewal still straight-lines the tower while firmness moves in the connection offer.{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,ACAD-DC-OUTAGE}} The peril is priced on the wrong loss cause.

Every flex-connected asset carries two balance sheets on the same connection. On the operations side, revenue is margin times utilization times survival — hourly economics that reprice when capacity tightens or a lawful interrupt removes a production hour. On the tower side, the renewal stack still straight-lines multi-year cover against a loss cause with almost no claims history.{{cite:BROK-MARSH-NIMBUS,SP-HYPERSCALE-INSURABLE-POOL}} Utilization is the premium; curtailment is the clawback. One ledger updates weekly; the other waits for physical damage.

We scored {{fact:total}} UK insurance-market participants ({{fact:l1}} carriers, {{fact:l2}} MGAs and brokers, {{fact:l3}} assets, {{fact:l4}} reinsurers) on Exposure to non-firm load and Preparedness to underwrite it, then reduced each to a single number: Margin of Safety = Preparedness − Exposure. The scatter plots posture, not hazard rank.

The scene-setting argument — collision, bought-not-sold, intelligence versus judgement, grid ahead of wording — is developed on Act I of the home page. This page picks up at the construct: how the bet is scored, what the live slice shows, and who can carry what the registers already reveal.

blocks.kicker: II · HOW LARGE IS THE BET

blocks.text: How large is the bet? Exposure is judgement work dressed as a number: how much curtailable load sits in the book or asset base, how correlated that concentration is when a constraint event bites more than one insured at once, and how far damage-first wordings miss the loss.{{cite:ACT-HHI-EIOPA,PRA-PPP}} Reading registers and mapping boundaries is intelligence. Deciding how much of that tail to keep net is judgement.

Five sub-factors carry the score: book concentration on energy and compute, non-firm intensity (from TEC gate status and embedded-capacity registers where measured), aggregation on shared grid geography, the trigger gap between damage-BI wordings and curtailment loss, and tenor mismatch between multi-year cover and a loss cause with almost no claims history. Each names a register fact the premium function currently ignores.

Book concentration asks how much revenue or premium sits in classes where curtailment can bite. Non-firm intensity is the MW-weighted share on Gate 1 or flagged flexible connections when registers are live. Aggregation is Herfindahl concentration of covered MW across grid supply points and constraint boundaries: the sub-factor that turns benign singles into a correlated event. Trigger gap is whether filed wording can pay lawful switch-off at all. Tenor mismatch captures multi-year policies against availability risk with almost no credible loss history.

Tenor mismatch bites hardest where the underlying asset runs spot-like availability economics inside a committed envelope. Hyperscale load contracts for always-on power and multi-year service levels while the connection that cleared may still carry Gate 1 curtailment rights.{{cite:NESO-TEC,NESO-CMP434}} The asset reprices utilization every constraint window; the policy reprices on renewal — if the trigger fires at all. Extended useful-life assumptions on infrastructure capex and extended policy terms on damage-BI both smooth a cash flow that does not smooth.

blocks.kicker: III · CAN THE FORM CARRY IT

blocks.text: Can this entity carry the risk it has written? Preparedness is not capital alone. It is whether the form, the data, and the pricing model treat curtailment as a first-class loss mechanism rather than a property-damage footnote.{{cite:LLOYDS-PARAMETRIC-CYBER,MGA-PARAMETRIX-SLA}} Product fit is the hinge: parametric availability triggers, SLA mirrors, and curtailment indices exist in fragments; most carrier wordings still wait for physical damage.

Underwriting expertise, telemetry, reinsurance depth, and pricing models must span power and interruption, not cat hazard footprints alone.{{cite:BROK-MARSH-NIMBUS,ACAD-BASIS-RISK-EXPECTILES}} In the competitive set, parametric MGAs and Lloyd's coverholders score highest on product fit: built for non-damage triggers. Composite carriers and wholesale brokers score on capital and market access but often carry a trigger gap on energy BI. Reinsurers score on tail capacity and cat modelling that does not transfer to curtailment geography. Preparedness maps who can structure the cover, not who writes the largest premium today.

{{fact:total}} entities on the current slice, split at the in-sample median (exposure ≥ {{fact:cut_exp}}, preparedness ≥ {{fact:cut_prep}}). Dot size = confidence; inner fill = measured share. A damage-first read would approve most of the field: {{fact:earning_pct}} plus {{fact:sidelined_pct}} sit in Earning it or Sidelined on exposure alone. Only {{fact:exposed_pct}} are Exposed on both axes, and {{fact:whitespace_pct}} sit in Whitespace where rated paper could deploy if the trigger gap closes.

blocks.text: A large positive margin on assessed inputs alone is a hypothesis, not a finding. The regression below plots Margin of Safety against each entity's measured/disclosed share: judgement on availability becomes intelligence as register tiers land. At {{fact:measured_pct}} blended measured share the slice remains PROVISIONAL; slope will move as Gate 2 status and ECR firmness propagate through the pipeline.

blocks.caption: Each dot is one entity. Measured share = scorable evidence-tier weight (measured, disclosed, derived) averaged across exposure and preparedness.

blocks.text: The stack carries different parts of the same correlated cluster. Carriers (L1) average a modest positive margin; underlying assets (L3) show the deepest negative spreads. Exposure on Gate-1 connections runs ahead of any single carrier's preparedness score.{{fact:l1}} carriers · {{fact:l2}} market participants · {{fact:l3}} assets · {{fact:l4}} reinsurers. Two surfaces in the data: placement posture above (L1/L2 skew toward Whitespace), register facts below (L3 skew toward Exposed).

Exposed mass concentrates in {{fact:exposed_heaviest_layer}}, structurally right because non-firm intensity is a register fact at Layer 3 before it propagates upward. Carriers and intermediaries sit more often in Whitespace ({{fact:whitespace_l1}} at Layer 1, {{fact:whitespace_l2}} at Layer 2) than in Exposed: balance-sheet preparedness is easier to evidence than curtailment exposure is to see from the outside. The placement question is not whether capacity exists. It is whether wordings match curtailment exposure before bind.

blocks.caption: Mean Margin of Safety by layer (±1 std dev in labels).

blocks.text: Segment tags (energy, data centre, parametric MGA, broker, reinsurance) expose where margin compresses. Data-centre and energy assets carry the most negative means; parametric and broker layers sit closer to neutral because product design already chases non-damage triggers. That split mirrors the two work surfaces: assets originate exposure; brokers and MGAs structure placement; carriers and reinsurers carry judgement on tail.

Energy generation and DC assets originate the exposure: negative margins where Gate 1 connections and SLA penalties outrun backup and monitoring. Parametric MGAs and specialist brokers sit closer to neutral; their products were designed for index triggers even when direct UK grid book is thin. Composite carriers span both, strong capital and mixed trigger fit. Segment means alongside layer means separate structural gaps (L1–L4) from thematic ones (who already sells generation 2.0 cover).

blocks.caption: Mean Margin of Safety by primary book segment (contract/entity_tags.json + layer inference).

blocks.text: At carrier level, exposure and preparedness diverge in ways the headline score hides. A syndicate with strong capital and weak register measurement can sit in whitespace on assessed inputs alone until Gate 2 status lands on a linked asset and the deterministic tier moves. Intelligence-heavy placement sees the headline; judgement-heavy underwriting needs the linked L3 strip.

Cat models are the wrong architecture: there is no licensable hazard module for lawful switch-off. The correlated loss is geographic and contractual, shared constraint boundaries and damage-only triggers, not a seismic zone or wind footprint.{{cite:ACAD-CRI-GRID-SRI,LMA-BI-GUIDE}}

Carrier-level comparison is an underwriting file, not a league table. Two syndicates with similar headline MoS can diverge on book concentration, trigger gap, and linked L3 dispersion. A whitespace carrier with strong parametric preparedness but thin energy premium is a different commercial target than an exposed composite stacking DC limits on damage BI. The scatter makes that divergence visible before placement, not after the first curtailment event.

Select a carrier: each dot is one underlying asset positioned by its Margin of Safety; the dashed line is the carrier average. A diversified renewable or DC book can look adequate at syndicate level while linked assets cluster exposed. That is the claims mirror in miniature: placement-side visibility before an adjuster opens the box-by-box review.

blocks.text: The market's conventional answer, property damage plus business interruption, fires on breakage. Curtailment loss is contractual: the operator exercises a lawful right to interrupt, the asset breaches an SLA, and revenue stops with the plant intact.{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,ACAD-BASIS-RISK-EXPECTILES}} When the notification arrives, adjusting is intelligence-heavy work on damage schedules. The loss already happened on the register.
Basis risk is not a modelling refinement. It is the gap between the loss and the trigger. Until availability is indexed to register-native measurement, every curtailment hour is an unfunded loss.

The loss shape is hourly, not episodic. When frontier capacity is scarce, buyers pay an elasticity premium for immediate availability — the option value of holding inventory against burst demand. Curtailment is the forced exercise of the opposite side: the hour is lost, the plant is intact, and revenue stops on a register notification rather than a trip. Damage-BI adjusts on schedules built for breakage; the economic loss already cleared in the operator portal.{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,ACAD-BASIS-RISK-EXPECTILES}} Weather indices and rack-level SLA mirrors can track uptime; neither indexes boundary curtailment probability against the firm baseline on the connection agreement.

blocks.caption: Two paths: damage-BI (left) pays; curtailment (right) often does not.

Normalised curtailment probability by NESO constraint boundary (measured, banked 2026-06-26). The correlated loss is geographic: Scotland and the South West run hottest; South Wales coolest.{{cite:NESO-CONSTRAINT-COSTS,NESO-CMP448}}
The cover attaches at the asset and travels up the tower. NFRI gives each level the same primary-source picture, priced.

items.name: Where the interrupt lands — assets on non-firm connections
items.role: Where the exposure sits: a non-firm, curtailable connection on a constrained boundary. The cover attaches here as parametric availability cover, the trigger calibrated to the asset's boundary curtailment probability and connection-gate status.
items.examples: Inputs: NESO TEC gate status, DNO flexible-connection share, boundary congestion. Cover: hours-of-availability index, indemnity per curtailed hour.

items.name: Who structures the gap — MGAs and brokers
items.role: Translate exposure into a placeable contract: set the parametric index, attachment and limit, and place the gap damage-based wordings leave open. NFRI is the underwriting file that justifies the rate to capacity.
items.examples: Uses: Margin-of-Safety rank, sub-factor decomposition, evidence tiers per rating.

items.name: Who carries the bet — carriers and syndicates
items.role: Hold the cover on balance sheet. NFRI flags where a book's exposure has run ahead of its preparedness — the negative Margin of Safety that surfaces accumulating risk before the loss history arrives.
items.examples: Uses: portfolio Margin-of-Safety distribution, book concentration, capital/reinsurance adequacy.

items.name: Who aggregates the tail — reinsurers and capacity
items.role: Stand behind the tower. The decisive question is correlation: how much non-firm exposure shares the same grid geography and curtails together. NFRI's aggregation factor prices that shared-boundary accumulation directly.
items.examples: Uses: aggregation-correlation over constraint boundaries, HHI on shared geography.

blocks.text: Four moves from trigger to settlement

blocks.caption: Parametric availability cover end to end — every step reads a primary source, not an adjuster's estimate.

steps.title: The interrupt
steps.detail: Measured loss of grid availability at the asset's constraint boundary — curtailment hours against the contracted firm baseline. Parametric, not damage-based.

steps.title: Size the bet
steps.detail: NFRI reads boundary curtailment probability and the entity's Exposure and Preparedness scores to size the bet and the capacity behind it.

steps.title: Price the gap
steps.detail: Rate is set on the Margin-of-Safety gap: exposure unmatched by preparedness is where loss concentrates and where the rate must rise.

steps.title: Settle on index
steps.detail: Payout is indexed to curtailment against the published trigger — settled in days, no physical-damage proof, no multi-month loss adjustment.{{cite:DESCARTES-DC-PARAMETRIC,REG-IAIS-PARAMETRIC}}

blocks.text: Register-native pricing

blocks.caption: From register row to rated trigger — the same evidence-tiered pipeline that scores the index sets the payout.

steps.title: Read the register
steps.detail: NESO TEC, DNO embedded-capacity registers and NESO congestion series — the measured base layer.{{cite:NESO-TEC,DCUSA-ECR}}

steps.title: Tag the evidence
steps.detail: Every input tagged measured, disclosed, derived or assessed — the honesty layer that gates publication.

steps.title: Fuse with judgement
steps.detail: Deterministic register reading fused with a sourced latent rating, weighted by credibility (λ by tier).{{cite:ACT-CREDIBILITY}}

steps.title: Exposure × preparedness
steps.detail: Two axes on 0–100; their difference is the Margin of Safety.

steps.title: Derive the rate
steps.detail: Trigger, rate and limit derived from the score and the boundary curtailment probability.

blocks.kicker: XII · THE WEDGE, NOT THE PRODUCT

blocks.text: The wedge argument — map as prerequisite, not product; fragments versus full stack — is developed in Act IV on the home page. What follows here is the operational close: levers, market fragments, and products already in force.

tabs.label: Five levers to close the gap

blocks.text: Brokers and MGAs have already placed parametric and SLA structures around DC and renewable risk. That is the line forming around the gap, not yet a full carrier stack.{{cite:BROK-MARSH-NIMBUS,MGA-PARAMETRIX-SLA}}

The competitive landscape is a stack of partial answers. Broker facilities (Nimbus-scale DC capacity, lifecycle placement) solve limit on damage-first forms. Parametric MGAs and coverholders (SLA mirrors, weather and uptime indices) solve trigger for rack-level telemetry but rarely index boundary curtailment. Composite carriers bring rated paper but inherit the trigger gap on energy BI. Reinsurers bring tail capacity but model cat geography, not shared constraint boundaries. No single market actor yet combines register-native measurement, basis-minimised availability trigger, aggregation-aware pricing, and balance-sheet scale. That is the whitespace the wedge is designed to illuminate.

blocks.caption: Market responses already in force — click through to source.

blocks.text: Gate 1 and Gate 2 made firmness a register fact, not a negotiating point.{{cite:NESO-CMP434}} CMP448 priced progression into the Gate-2 queue from January 2026.{{cite:NESO-CMP448}} Demand-side reform is consulting on curtailment rights for the largest users. The rules landed before the market repriced who can carry the interruptible half. Registers move; damage triangles lag. That is the platform shift: business model transformation, not another hazard score.

Brokers have placed billion-dollar DC facilities on non-firm terms; the constraint cost curve is observable in NESO data while BI rates on damage triggers stay flat. Rising physical cost and flat premium on the wrong loss cause is mispricing by architecture, not by ignorance.

Compute build-out is not waiting for firm connections, and power is the binding constraint on both sides of the same queue.{{cite:INDUSTRY-DC-COMPUTE-DEMAND,OFGEM-DEMAND-REFORM}} Operators cannot run legacy headroom and new load at full nameplate when the boundary binds — replacement timing for capacity is driven by what the grid can firm, not by wear alone. Demand-side reform will make curtailment rights explicit for the largest users just as constraint costs enter NESO charging.{{cite:NESO-CONSTRAINT-COSTS,NESO-CMP448}} The implied curve for availability does not yet exist in the tower; the register facts that would construct it already do.
